lesson.title: El Espectáculo de Diez: A Count-to-Ten Performance for Sol
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Today is your solo show — you get to count all the way to diez for Sol, all by yourself, while everyone watches and listens!
Take a deep breath and count out loud from uno all the way to diez, nice and clear, using a big movement for each número if you like.
When you reach diez, take a bow — Sol and the whole class cheer for you! Then try it again, maybe even faster.
You counted all the way to diez by yourself — uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez! Next week, get ready to learn colors in Spanish.

questions.q: Grown-up, read aloud: 🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵 Is this seis or siete?
Grown-up, read aloud: 🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵 Is this siete or ocho?
Grown-up, read aloud: 🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵🔵 Is this nueve or diez?
Grown-up, read aloud: Sol holds up a card with a number on it. What word means 'number' — el número or el amigo?

objectives: Count aloud from uno to diez independently, with minimal prompting, as a short performance
Recall and use número in a cumulative review of week 4's numbers
materialsNeeded: An imaginary or real stage — a rug or a chair works fine
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Set up a little 'stage' — a rug or a favorite spot — for your child's counting performance.
2. Have your child take a deep breath and count out loud from uno all the way to diez for Sol and the audience.
3. Encourage a big movement on each number if your child wants to bring back a favorite from earlier in the week.
4. Cheer loudly and clap when your child reaches diez, then invite a bow.
5. Repeat once or twice more, letting your child try counting faster or with different movements each time.
6. Complete the on-screen multiple-choice review together, reading each question aloud since your child may not read yet.
7. Close the show: take a bow together and wave to Sol.
differentiationTips: Struggling: count alongside your child quietly rather than having them perform fully solo
Ready for more: challenge your child to count to diez and then immediately back down to uno
This is a celebration lesson — the goal is confident, joyful counting your child already practiced this week, not teaching anything brand new
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a cumulative spoken counting performance — success looks like your child counting from uno to diez aloud with some independence, with prompting as needed. In the multiple-choice game: 6 dots → seis, 8 dots → ocho, 10 dots → diez, and el número means 'number'.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Closes week 4's WA-WL-2015.1.3 Presentational Speaking arc with the clearest possible assessment of the target — an unprompted, audience-facing solo count from uno to diez — bringing together every number from this week and last into one connected performance, exactly the scope-and-sequence's own design for this Day 5.
